quizzes.title: Key terms and ideas
quizzes.intro: Ten quick checks on fixed cost, utilities, dyes and set-up as the dyeing costing sheet defines them.

questions.q: The fixed cost per minute of a machine is made up of
questions.explain: The lecture lists depreciation, finance and labour as the fixed cost per minute. Steam and power are the utilities cost; dyes are charged separately by shade.

questions.q: The utilities cost per minute is charged for
options: Neither; it is a cost per metre
questions.explain: Utilities apply only to running: the machine consumes steam and power while fabric passes. Fixed cost, by contrast, applies to both set-up and running.

questions.q: The fixed cost per minute applies to set-up minutes as well as to running minutes.
questions.explain: The machine, its finance and its operators cost the same per minute whether it is being set up or running, so fixed cost covers both.

questions.q: For an order of L metres on a machine running at a given speed, the running minutes are
questions.explain: Running minutes = L ÷ speed: 10,000 m at 120 m/min takes 83.3 minutes, as in the bleaching row. Set-up minutes are added separately.

questions.q: Which shade carries dyes and chemicals of Rs 15 per metre run?
questions.explain: The rates are Rs 3, 8, 15 and 25 per metre for light, medium, dark and extra dark respectively.

questions.q: The set-up quantity of colour for a medium shade is worth
questions.explain: Set-up colour is worth 300 m of running dyes: 300 × Rs 8 = Rs 2,400 for medium. Rs 900 is light and Rs 4,500 dark.

questions.q: In the sheet, bleaching and mercerising each carry a dyes-and-chemicals cost per metre that depends on the shade.
questions.explain: Their totals are simply fixed per metre plus utilities per metre (0.953 + 0.839 = 1.79 for bleaching). Only the dyeing processes carry the shade-dependent dyes cost.

questions.q: Which processes in the sheet carry the shade-dependent dyes cost?
options: Thermosol, pad steam and stenter dyeing
questions.explain: These three are the dyeing processes, and each shows about Rs 28–29 per metre, of which the dyes are Rs 25.75. The others are preparation and finishing steps costing a few rupees.

questions.q: The lecture calls this sheet 'the ABC lesson of Lecture 12 turned into a quotation tool'. ABC stands for
questions.explain: Activity-based costing traces costs to the activities that cause them; here set-up minutes and set-up colour are order-level activities charged to the order that triggers them.

questions.q: In this lecture a 'route' is
options: The set of machines running at the same time
The sequence of processes a fabric passes through, costed by adding each process's Rs per metre
The shade selected in the drop-down
questions.explain: Route 1, for example, is bleach → merc → pad steam → stenter finishing, and its Rs 35.94 is the sum of those four rows.

quizzes.title: Formulas and relationships
quizzes.intro: How fixed, utilities and dyes costs per metre are built, and which way each moves with speed, order size and shade.

questions.q: Fixed cost per metre for a process on an order of L metres is
questions.explain: Fixed cost accrues through both set-up and running, so the whole occupation time is multiplied by the rate and spread over the metres. Leaving out set-up understates the cost.

questions.q: Utilities cost per metre equals
questions.explain: Utilities Rs/min × (L ÷ speed) ÷ L = Rs/min ÷ speed. Order size cancels out because utilities apply only to running time.

questions.q: The utilities cost per metre of a process does not change with the order size.
questions.explain: It reduces to utilities Rs/min ÷ speed; every metre takes the same fraction of a minute whatever the order length. Only the set-up-related costs depend on L.

questions.q: As the order size falls, the fixed cost per metre of a process
options: Rises, because the set-up minutes are spread over fewer metres
questions.explain: The running part (Rs/min ÷ speed) is constant, but set-up minutes × Rs/min is a lump that becomes larger per metre as L shrinks.

questions.q: Dyes and chemicals per metre for a given shade on an order of L metres are
options: Running rate + set-up colour value ÷ L
questions.explain: For extra dark on 10,000 m: 25 + 7,500 ÷ 10,000 = Rs 25.75 per metre, which is the dyes figure hidden inside the Rs 29.26 thermosol total.

questions.q: If a machine's speed is doubled (same Rs/min), its utilities cost per metre
questions.explain: Utilities per metre = Rs/min ÷ speed, so twice the speed means half the minutes per metre and half the cost.

questions.q: Moving from dark to extra dark raises the dyes cost per metre by exactly Rs 10 whatever the order size.
questions.explain: The running rate rises by Rs 10, but the set-up colour also rises from Rs 4,500 to Rs 7,500, adding another Rs 3,000 ÷ L per metre — Rs 0.30 at 10,000 m, Rs 1.50 at 2,000 m.

questions.q: For a very large order, which part of the dyeing cost per metre becomes negligible?
options: The set-up colour spread per metre
The running part of the fixed cost
questions.explain: Set-up colour ÷ L (and set-up minutes × Rs/min ÷ L) shrink towards zero as L grows; the running rates per metre stay exactly the same.

questions.q: The total Rs per metre of a process in the sheet is
options: Fixed per metre + utilities per metre + dyes per metre
The route total divided by the number of processes
questions.explain: Column I adds the three per-metre components; for bleaching the dyes component is zero, so 0.953 + 0.839 = 1.79.

questions.q: A process shows 142.9 running minutes for an order of 10,000 m. Its speed is
questions.explain: Speed = 10,000 ÷ 142.9 = 70 m/min, the pad steam, sanforizing and washing speed in the sheet. 50 m/min would give 200 minutes.

quizzes.title: Worked calculations
quizzes.intro: Build fixed, utilities and dyes costs per metre for new orders and add them up by process and by route.

questions.q: An order of 12,000 m runs on a machine at 60 m/min. Running minutes?
That machine has a fixed cost of Rs 80 per minute and needs 40 set-up minutes. Fixed cost per metre for the 12,000 m order, to the nearest paisa?
Its utilities cost is Rs 45 per minute at 60 m/min. Utilities cost per metre?
The 12,000 m order is a dark shade (Rs 15 per metre run, set-up colour Rs 4,500). Dyes and chemicals per metre, to three decimals?
Total cost per metre of that dyeing process (fixed 1.60 + utilities 0.75 + dyes 15.375), to two decimals?
An extra dark order of only 2,000 m (Rs 25 per metre run, set-up colour Rs 7,500). Dyes and chemicals per metre?
Using the sheet's rounded figures, bleaching Rs 1.79, mercerizing Rs 1.87 and stenter dyeing Rs 28.47 per metre, what is the route total of bleach → merc → stenter dyeing?
questions.explain: 1.79 + 1.87 + 28.47 = Rs 32.13 per metre (the sheet shows 32.14 because it adds unrounded values).

questions.q: Bleaching runs at 120 m/min with fixed cost Rs 90 per minute and 20 set-up minutes. Fixed cost per metre on 10,000 m, to the nearest paisa?
A medium shade on a 5,000 m order: dyes and chemicals per metre are
questions.explain: 8 + 2,400 ÷ 5,000 = 8 + 0.48 = Rs 8.48. Rs 8.00 ignores the set-up colour; Rs 8.24 uses 10,000 m; Rs 10.40 uses 1,000 m.

questions.q: Fixed Rs 100 per minute, running 125 min, set-up 30 min, order 10,000 m. By how much does ignoring the set-up minutes understate the fixed cost per metre?

quizzes.title: Applied in practice
quizzes.intro: Quotation-desk decisions: which route, what happens on small orders, and the mistakes that lose money.

questions.q: Of the five routes costed in the sheet for 10,000 m, the cheapest is
options: Route 3: bleach → pad steam → stenter finishing
Route 1: bleach → merc → pad steam → stenter finishing
Route 2: bleach → merc → thermosol → wash → stenter finishing
questions.explain: Route 4 costs Rs 30.26 per metre: two processes, and stenter dyeing both dyes and finishes. Route 3 is Rs 34.07, route 1 Rs 35.94 and route 2 Rs 39.36.

questions.q: Route 2 is the most expensive at Rs 39.36 per metre mainly because
options: Thermosol dyeing is dearer than pad steam and the route adds a washing step
It is quoted at the extra dark shade only
questions.explain: Thermosol (29.26) exceeds pad steam (28.59) and washing adds Rs 2.74. All routes are costed at the same shade.

questions.q: A customer reduces an order from 10,000 m to 2,000 m. What happens to the quotation per metre?
options: Only the utilities per metre rise
The bleaching cost per metre rises five-fold
Nothing; costs per metre are fixed by the sheet
The dyeing processes rise by several rupees a metre because set-up minutes and set-up colour are spread over a fifth of the length
questions.explain: The lecture gives exactly this example. Set-up colour alone goes from Rs 0.75 to Rs 3.75 per metre for extra dark; running costs per metre are unchanged.

questions.q: The bleaching cost per metre in the sheet is the same whichever shade is selected.
questions.explain: Bleaching has no dyes component; its Rs 1.79 is fixed plus utilities. Shade only changes the three dyeing rows.

questions.q: A merchandiser quotes a 1,000 m sample order at the same Rs per metre as 10,000 m bulk. The likely result is
options: A fair quotation, since the processes are identical
The set-up minutes and set-up colour are under-recovered and the sample order loses money
questions.explain: At 1,000 m the extra dark set-up colour alone is Rs 7.50 per metre instead of Rs 0.75, and set-up minutes per metre are ten times larger. The bulk price cannot cover them.

questions.q: Extra dark set-up colour is Rs 7,500. How much more does it add per metre on a 2,000 m order than on a 10,000 m order?
A buyer asks for a mercerised finish on route 3 (bleach → pad steam → stenter finishing). By how much does the quotation per metre rise?
questions.explain: Adding mercerising turns route 3 into route 1: 34.07 + 1.87 = 35.94. Rs 1.79 is bleaching; Rs 3.66 adds both.

questions.q: The mill raises the stenter dyeing speed from 80 to 100 m/min. Which cost components per metre fall?
options: Utilities per metre and the running part of the fixed cost per metre
None; the Rs/min rates are unchanged
The running dye rate per metre
questions.explain: Both are Rs/min ÷ speed, so a higher speed means fewer minutes per metre. The dye rate per metre run and the set-up lumps do not depend on speed.

questions.q: Route 5 costs Rs 1.88 per metre more than route 4. That extra money buys
questions.explain: Route 5 is route 4 with mercerising inserted: 30.26 + 1.87 ≈ 32.14 (the sheet adds unrounded values).

questions.q: Calender and sanforizing are included in at least one of the five route totals.
questions.explain: They are costed in rows 10 and 11 (Rs 0.86 and 0.43) but none of the five listed routes uses them; they would be added if the customer's finish required them.

quizzes.title: Challenge review
quizzes.intro: Harder two-step costing across order sizes, shades and speeds, plus the errors a checker should catch.

questions.q: Thermosol: 50 m/min, fixed Rs 85/min, utilities Rs 52/min, 90 set-up minutes, extra dark (Rs 25 run, set-up colour Rs 7,500). Total Rs per metre for 2,000 m, to two decimals?
The same thermosol process and shade on a 10,000 m order. Total Rs per metre, to two decimals?
questions.explain: Run 200 min; fixed = 85 × 290 ÷ 10,000 = 2.465; utilities 1.04; dyes = 25 + 0.75 = 25.75. Total 29.255 ≈ Rs 29.26 — about Rs 6 less than the 2,000 m order.

questions.q: In the two thermosol answers above the 2,000 m order costs about Rs 6 per metre more. Which two items cause the whole difference?
options: Fixed cost of the set-up minutes and the set-up colour
Utilities per metre and the running dye rate
questions.explain: Set-up minutes: 85 × 90 × (1/2,000 − 1/10,000) = Rs 3.06; set-up colour: 7,500 × (1/2,000 − 1/10,000) = Rs 3.00. Utilities and running dyes per metre are identical on both orders.

questions.q: For a dark shade (set-up colour Rs 4,500), at what order size does the set-up colour add exactly Rs 1.50 per metre?
questions.explain: 4,500 ÷ L = 1.50 gives L = 3,000 m. 1,500 m would give Rs 3.00; 30,000 m only Rs 0.15.

questions.q: Doubling the order size halves the total cost per metre of a dyeing process.
questions.explain: Only the set-up components (set-up minutes × Rs/min and set-up colour) halve per metre. Utilities per metre, running fixed cost per metre and the running dye rate do not change.

questions.q: A light shade (Rs 3 per metre run, set-up colour Rs 900) on a 25,000 m order. Dyes and chemicals per metre, to three decimals?
questions.explain: 3 + 900 ÷ 25,000 = 3 + 0.036 = Rs 3.036 per metre; on a long light-shade order the set-up colour is almost invisible.

questions.q: A trainee charged utilities (Rs 50/min) on set-up minutes too: running 125 min, set-up 30 min, 10,000 m. The utilities per metre are overstated by
Utilities cost Rs 45 per minute. What running speed in m/min would bring utilities down to Rs 0.50 per metre?
questions.explain: Utilities per metre = 45 ÷ speed = 0.50, so speed = 45 ÷ 0.50 = 90 m/min.

questions.q: Route 3 costs Rs 34.07 per metre at extra dark on 10,000 m. If the shade is changed to dark (Rs 15 run, set-up colour Rs 4,500), the route cost becomes about
questions.explain: Only pad steam's dyes change: (25 − 15) + (7,500 − 4,500) ÷ 10,000 = 10 + 0.30 = Rs 10.30 less, so 34.07 − 10.30 = Rs 23.77. Rs 24.07 forgets the set-up colour.

questions.q: Which statement about the sheet's time columns is correct?
options: Running minutes equal order size ÷ speed, while set-up minutes are fixed per order
Utilities are charged on set-up minutes
Dyes per metre are independent of order size
Set-up minutes scale with the order size
questions.explain: Running time is proportional to metres; set-up is a lump per order. That is why per-metre costs fall as orders grow. Dyes per metre include set-up colour ÷ L, so they do depend on order size.
